claims.claim: bladderwort trap investment stops in deep shade (Adamec 2015)
claims.source_value: Adamec concludes that at very low CO₂ and in deep shade the low photosynthetic rate and apical growth, with very high shoot N and P, prevent trap production; the shade evidence he cites is U. foliosa producing no traps at 10 % of open irradiance (Bern 1997) and strongly shaded U. vulgaris (Englund & Harms 2003)
claims.location: p. 145 (PDF p. 17), Discussion and conclusion; p. 144 (PDF p. 16), Discussion
claims.quote: deep shade conditions, the resulting low photosynthetic rate … prevent trap production
claims.conditions: his own experiment did not vary light: a 12–14-day experiment in a naturally lit greenhouse (from 14 June 2012) with U. vulgaris, U. australis and U. reflexa at 26–42 % of open irradiance, crossing high (0.30–0.58 mM) or low (0.024–0.062 mM) free CO₂ with prey or no prey
claims.note: The statement is Adamec's synthesis resting on Bern 1997 and Englund & Harms 2003; the rewrite could cite 'Adamec 2015, reviewing Bern 1997 and Englund & Harms 2003'. His own result is about CO₂: CO₂ addition raised mean trap dry weight 2.7–249 times and the investment in carnivory in all three species, while prey addition had a much smaller effect.

notes: Also useful for §3.4.7: in most studies, more mineral nutrient (prey capture, higher NH4, NO3, PO4 in the water) lowered the investment in carnivory by negative feedback, with shoot N or P content the regulator (Bern 1997; Kibriya & Jones 2007), p. 144. Aquatic Utricularia biomass doubles in 5–20 days, apical growth 1–4.2 nodes per day (p. 133).
